bifurcation.note: Declared before any image was opened. Every visual judgement here is a DECISIONS question — whether a region owns a palette, a silhouette, a prop vocabulary and a named feature — not a rendering question. The only reference images cited are Morrowind's own region screenshots at corpus/70-visual/refs/morrowind/REF-A21-regions/ (39 files, MANIFEST metrics_valid_for: ["art-direction"], pixel_metrics_valid: false for all 39, which is exactly the flag that permits their use here and forbids their use for fidelity). No modern AAA screenshot is cited anywhere and no fidelity claim is made. Two fidelity-flavoured observations (textureMB 0, no contact shadows) are recorded in secondary_observations as observations only and carry no score.

reference_items.why_not_ten: The fix was bought with earthworks the item does not measure. My own cut/fill probe (critic-road-cutfill.json, WorldField with and without setRoads, 3 m sub-sampling) gives a tallest embankment of 17.52 m on stormhold-helstrom at (2240.3,1340.2) and a deepest cutting of 3.62 m at (2113.9,1218.6) — the latter above scale-audit's own <=3.5 m pass bar, which reads 3.0 m only because it samples at the 12 m road points. Then either re-solve the deck in tools/world/build-roads.mjs so no fill exceeds 4 m, or emit the 21 deck_spans as real geometry that game/src/render reads, so a 16 m viaduct is a structure the player walks over rather than a hill the terrain grew.

reference_items.why_not_ten: M17 is a HUMAN test and this is the first round in which it could be taken, because the pack is now honestly shuffled. On 8 of the 39 brightest frames I scored 4/8 (m17-blind-answers-critic-r2.json, written before the reveal) against a pass bar of >=33/39 (85%) and a fail floor of <28/39 (72%). Three of the four misses are the same miss: frames 023, 042 and 050 are the STONE WASTES ('glassed salt crust', glass_thorn, whale_bone_frame, salt_block_wall, crater_rim) and I called all three Marauder's Coast, because what is rendered is a khaki flat under a white fog band with no glass, no bone frame and no crater. The fourth is frame-017, the DEEP MARSHES ('violet-black silt and voriplasm margin', corpse_lily, drowned_tree, drowned_xanmeer_tooth, green fever-fog), rendered as a bright green lawn with ball-canopy trees. M19 is 0/13: every region's ONLY-HERE element (welkynd_pillar x34, petrified_bole x400, rock_flute_spire x14, glassed_crater x16, beached_hull_house x12 ...) is an integer literal in tools/world/build-regions.mjs and not one instance is placed — the live scene has entitiesLive 0 in all thirteen regions and the whole province renders with textureMB 0 and 17 materials. M20 is 0 (audioMB 0). M21 is 0 (no roster placed). M18 passes at the >=6 bar with three pairs at exactly 6, and five of its nine declared axes — fauna, architecture, audio, weather, hazard — are DROPPED rather than measured, which is an honest statement that they are not implemented.
reference_items.path_to_ten: (a) Give each region a second and third prop class beyond the shared canopy+under+rock lattice, and place its ONLY-HERE element as real instances at the declared counts, so M19 reads 13/13 with >=8 instances in-region and 0 elsewhere. (b) Ship the five dropped M18 axes as measurable properties: an architecture mesh set, a fauna set, an ambient bed, a weather state machine and a firing hazard per region. (c) Re-run M17 with a fresh judge on the full 117-frame pack and clear >=33/39 by day and >=27/39 at night. (d) Close the night pass specifically: ours_night leave-one-out is 33.3% (raw descriptor) and 25.6% once exposure is removed, against M17 step 6's explicit >=70%.

reference_items.why_not_ten: The province has 466 m of vertical range (-41.8 to +424.2) and none of it constrains anything, because THERE IS NO MAXIMUM WALKABLE SLOPE. critic-loco-probe.json L1: holding the walk stick straight uphill on a 70.63 deg face climbs 10.28 m in 5 s; on a 66.20 deg face, 16.76 m; state never leaves WALK, stamina 120->120, HP 620->620. The province's own passability model — the S9-NO-FENCES flood fill in scale-audit.mjs — calls slope > 40 deg impassable, so two instruments in this piece disagree by 30 degrees and neither was asked to reconcile. L2: dropped from 150 m above ground the player arrives at 620/620 HP having never left state WALK. The Salt Hills' 'snow visible on unreachable peaks' is reachable, and every cliff in Valus Ridge is a ramp. M36-ROAD-RELIEF is 27.3% against a 30% target (fail floor 12).
reference_items.path_to_ten: Declare a walkable-slope ceiling in game/src/combat/player.js and enforce it against field.slopeAt: above 40 deg the capsule slides rather than climbs, and above ~55 deg it is not traversable at all. Re-run S9-NO-FENCES with the capsule rather than a flood fill and report the two numbers together. Then run RI-WLD07's 12-high-point landmark-silhouette check and the >=120 climbable-features count, which have still never been run, and route trunk metreage through Valus Ridge / Salt Hills / Stone Forest to clear 30% relief without carving marsh.

M58 (tell >=2.0 s and >=15 m before damage), M59 (>=80 s to death, <=6.0 s escape), M60 (>=2 working counters each) and M61-M62 are all unmeasurable because there is nothing to measure.

blind_comparisons.question: Given the thirteen region names and their ground / flora / architecture / climate descriptor columns, and nothing else, which region is each unlabelled frame?
blind_comparisons.blind_rationale: M17 is a self-identification test, not a two-sided A/B, so blind_pick is 'none'. I judged 8 frames chosen by luminance computed from the pixels, wrote the calls and my reasons to disk, then revealed by script: 4/8. Two of the four correct calls (Clay Moor's fired red pan, Valus Ridge's limestone scree and thorn pine) came from something the region owns; one (The Hive) was a palette guess that happened to land. Three of the four misses are one miss: frames 023, 042 and 050 are the Stone Wastes and I called all three Marauder's Coast, because a glassed salt crust with whale-bone frames and a crater rim renders as a khaki flat under a white fog band. The fourth is the Deep Marshes rendered as a green lawn.

rerun.harsher_lens: Because the machine analogue disagreed with the human read (74.4% against 50%), I rebuilt the instrument three ways rather than accepting either number: raw 4x4 CIELAB, the same with per-image exposure removed, and chroma-only. Then I built the matched design the shipped comparison never had — 9 regions x 3 images, 200 random draws, on both populations, so region count, images per region and chance level are identical.
rerun.additional_measurement: A structure-only descriptor: 6x4 Sobel edge density plus 6x4 luminance layout, z-scored per image, so colour and exposure carry nothing. Ours_day LOO falls 74.4% -> 30.8% and Fisher 3.10 -> 1.77; Morrowind falls 25.6% -> 17.9%. Roughly two-thirds of our measured region separability is colour.

ar1.not_applicable_reason: No fight occurs in this piece and entitiesLive is 0 in all thirteen regions, so A1-A5, A8 and A10 have no encounter to run against. A6, A7 and A9 were run anyway and pass.

checks.observed: ar2-b1-hud-exploring.png, Lilmoth, 12:00, exploring, UI visible: no arrow, pin, waypoint, compass, distance readout or edge indicator anywhere in the frame.

The travel network is not a map-pin menu. Every service refuses unless its road has been walked ('You have not walked the stormhold-thorn road. No one sells passage over ground you have not crossed.'), costs gold, moves the player along a real route at a mode-specific speed, and ends 14 m from a station marker rather than at any objective. 29 of 68 services were still refused after four legs were walked.

biggest_gap.what: All thirteen regions are the same three primitives — canopy, under, rock — recoloured, and not one of the thirteen declared ONLY-HERE elements exists in the world. Every region in game/data/world/regions.json carries the identical prop schema `canopy+under+rock`, drawing on seven shared canopy shapes and five shared under shapes; the whole 14.31 km2 province renders with textureMB 0, atlasCount 0, 17 materials and 8 programs. `only_here: {id, instances}` — welkynd_pillar x34, petrified_bole x400, rock_flute_spire x14, glassed_crater x16, beached_hull_house x12 and nine more — is an integer literal in tools/world/build-regions.mjs and nothing places an instance, so RI-WLD04 M19 measures 0 of 13. Five of M18's nine axes (fauna, architecture, audio, weather, hazard) are DROPPED rather than measured, which is the same statement in the instrument's own words. The consequence is measurable two ways. A human taking M17 on the now-honest pack scores 4/8 against a pass bar of 85%, and three of the four misses are one miss: frames 023, 042 and 050 are the Stone Wastes — 'glassed salt crust', glass_thorn, whale_bone_frame, salt_block_wall, crater_rim — and all three read as Marauder's Coast, because what is rendered is a khaki flat under a white fog band. And with colour and exposure removed from the machine descriptor, leave-one-out identification falls 74.4% -> 30.8% and Fisher 3.10 -> 1.77: about two-thirds of the measured region separability is carried by tint alone, which is RI-WLD04's own named way to lose.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: S24 rules that thirteen regions must each read as a different place and that an implementation where everything is one terrain with a recoloured fog has failed regardless of how good the terrain is — and a player walking the 6.6 km crossing passes through five regions that differ in ground colour and in nothing they can name.

remedy.action: Place the ONLY-HERE elements as real instances, and give each region at least one prop class that no other region has. Concretely: (1) extend the region prop schema in tools/world/build-regions.mjs and game/src/world/province.js beyond `canopy+under+rock` with a fourth slot `signature`, carrying its own mesh generator per region — a welkynd pillar for Blackwood, a rock-flute spire for Valus Ridge, a whale-bone frame and crater rim for the Stone Wastes, a beached hull house and tide pole for Marauder's Coast, a drowned xanmeer tooth and corpse lily for the Deep Marshes, a stilt row and tideway marker for the Eastern Rootlands; (2) place them at the counts regions.json already declares, from the same seeded lattice the existing props use, so the number in the table becomes the number in the world; (3) add a `signature_silhouette` axis and an `architecture_placed` axis to tools/world/region-axes.mjs, computed from placed instances rather than from a table row, and un-drop `architecture`; (4) give the ground more than one material — at present textureMB is 0, so albedo is a per-region constant and RI-WLD04's 'albedo must come from different materials, not a LUT' cannot be satisfied at all.
remedy.acceptance: RI-WLD04 M19 reads 13/13: each region's ONLY-HERE element is queryable in the running world at >=8 instances inside its own region and 0 instances in every other region. AND the structure-only re-measurement (critic-structure-only.json, colour and exposure removed) rises from 30.8% to >=55% leave-one-out on the 39 day frames, so region identity survives having the tint taken away. AND M18 measures >=7 axes on every one of the 78 pairs with `architecture` un-dropped and computed from placed instances.

The road fix is an earthwork wearing a viaduct's name. roads.json declares 21 deck_spans totalling 2,494 m, eleven of them kind 'viaduct' up to 16 m tall on stormhold-helstrom and three 'causeway over water' on blackrose-lilmoth; grep across game/src finds deck_spans read nowhere. In the built world the deck is produced by _applyRoads blending the ground toward the deck height over hw..3.2*hw, so a 16 m viaduct is a 16 m ridge of the same material as the hillside. 2,537 of my sampled shoulder points exceed 40 degrees, peaking at 70.6 degrees at (2286.3, 1360.9). shot-embankment-stormhold-helstrom-air.png shows what it looks like: a smooth grey berm through The Stone Forest with no road surface, no parapet, no structure and no track.

The player can walk off a 29.22 m drop and take nothing. critic-road-probe.json R2 at the 17.5 m fill on stormhold-helstrom: walking east 20 m descends 29.22 m onto a 66.2 degree face, state WALK throughout, HP 620 -> 620. So the embankment is not a fence — but only because nothing about height costs anything.

__HARNESS.camera(pose) accepts an unrecognised pose object and silently freezes the camera instead of throwing. camera({yaw, pitch, arm}) matches no branch, so `cur` is taken from the live rig and written back as an override; every later call then reads `cur` from that override, and six frames captured across 25-500 m of teleporting came out from one position. HARNESS.md R7 says every method either does the thing or throws. This one does neither.

Standing water is rendered as an untextured flat polygon with no shoreline, no specular and no depth cue. shot-tideway-lilmoth-archon.png is taken standing in 0.181 m of water (surface_y 1.611 over ground_y 1.430, band W1, substrate SUCK) in the Eastern Rootlands and no water is visible in the frame at all; blind-frames/frame-042.png shows the other case, where 8 m of water reads as a flat grey hexagon lying on the mud. Since S25 makes depth readable off the player's own silhouette, water the player cannot see is a seam problem as well as a rendering one.

corpus_extended.what: RI-WLD01 has no clause requiring a road to have a road's gradient. Its 'How we lose' list catches friction-cheating, sinuosity-forgetting, ocean bloat and (since round 1) drowned roads, and it cannot see a trunk leg that rises 19.63 m over an 11.99 m run. Proposed check M2c — ROAD GRADE: no trunk segment above 0.12 grade except a declared 'stair' or 'switchback' class, sub-sampled at 3 m, all ten legs. Also proposed: M2-ROAD-CUT-AND-FILL must sub-sample at 3 m rather than at the 12 m road points, because at road-point resolution it reads 3.0 m where the terrain is 3.62 m — the check's own sampling rate is currently what decides its result.

The machine analogue of M17 that this project has been using — a 4x4 grid of mean CIELAB — is satisfied by a per-region colour grade, which is the item's own named way to lose. It reads 74.4% where a human judge reads 50% on the same frames. Proposed: the analogue must be reported alongside a STRUCTURE-ONLY control in which colour and exposure carry nothing (z-scored Sobel edge density plus luminance layout), and the item's pass condition on the analogue must be stated on the control, not on the colour descriptor. Second proposal: A7's comparison against Morrowind must be run on a MATCHED design — equal region count, equal images per region, equal chance level, averaged over random draws — because ours-13x9 against Morrowind-9x4.33 is not a comparison, and because pooling three lighting conditions on our side and none on theirs is what produced the Fisher 1.005 headline.

RI-WLD07 measures how much vertical range the province HAS and never asks whether any of it constrains movement. There is no maximum-walkable-slope check anywhere in the corpus, and the build walks 70.63 degrees at full speed while its own S9-NO-FENCES flood fill calls 40 degrees impassable. Proposed check: MAX-WALKABLE-SLOPE — hold the walk stick uphill at the ten steepest in-region points and assert horizontal progress falls to zero above a declared ceiling, and require S9-NO-FENCES to be re-run with the capsule so the two instruments agree.

arbitration_questions.question: Does S17 ('the hour comes from distance, never from slow walking') permit off-road substrate and water bands to reduce walk speed?
arbitration_questions.souls_side: Walk speed is a Souls-side property tuned for combat spacing at 2.0 m/s and S17 says it may not be lowered to inflate traversal time; the build now realises 1.8632 m/s on dry SUCK and 1.7000 m/s in W2, which is a 6.8-15% reduction with no water involved in the first case.
arbitration_questions.morrowind_side: S25 makes water a genuine tactical terrain that costs something to be in, and RI-WLD10's band ladder specifies exact speeds per band; a marsh where mud costs nothing is not a marsh. The crossing itself measures mean 1.9998 m/s, so no part of the canonical hour is bought with friction.

Every one of them is scored fail-closed or partial in the harsher direction, never omitted and never averaged away. Escalation ladder, all five rungs: (1) ZOOM — re-sampled the road at 3 m instead of at its 12 m points, which turned a passing cut check into a failing one, and z-scored the visual descriptor per cell instead of taking a pooled Fisher; (2) CHANGE THE SAMPLE — took the region frames the pack's own luminance said were brightest rather than the first thirteen, and probed the ugliest legs rather than the crossing; (3) STRESS — walked uphill at 70 degrees, dropped from 150 m, stood 60 s in 8 m of water and 60 s in all thirteen hazard regions, swept burden to 120%; (4) SECOND-ORDER PROPERTY — not 'do the regions differ' but 'do they differ when you take the colour away', which is where the 74.4% became 30.8%; (5) FIRST MINUTE AND TENTH HOUR — the first minute is a green lawn that is meant to be the Deep Marshes, the tenth hour is a province where nothing you can name belongs to anywhere.

ORDERING. I read no prior verdict, no builder status file and no gap-ledger entry until after every raw measurement in this document existed on disk. The one exception is deliberate and is the assignment itself: I was told in my brief that round 1 had found a drowned road and an unshuffled pack, so the first two things I measured were the road-water audit and the pack's shuffle statistics. I did not read corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/W1-01.md's per-item scores until the numbers above were written.

ROUND 1 IS VOID, AND MOST OF IT SURVIVES ANYWAY. `node tools/verdict-validate.mjs corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/W1-01.json` fails with two errors: reports/region-shots/frame-01.png and frame-39.png do not exist, because the pack was rebuilt. That is a formal VOID under CRITIC-DOCTRINE §1.2 and it is a process defect on round 1's side, not on the remediation's: a verdict must copy every artifact it cites into its own directory, and round 1 cited two at transient reports/ paths. I have copied every frame I cite. What the void does NOT do is unmake round 1's findings, and I re-tested them independently rather than inheriting them. Surviving on my own evidence: the crossing is a real walk at an honest speed (re-measured, 55.356 min, mean 1.9998 m/s); the M18 axes were config reads (the rebuilt tool now names its sources and drops five axes rather than scoring them, which is an admission); the blind pack was unshuffled (the rebuilt pack is shuffled, and I recomputed its statistics); the road ran under water (fixed, and I recomputed the fix from the terrain). Not surviving: round 1's 8/10 on RI-WLD01, because the remedy introduced a 58.6-degree grade; and its 5/10 on RI-WLD04, because it never took M17 on an honest pack and never ran M19.

THE FISHER 3.01 -> 1.005 QUESTION, RESOLVED. Both readings offered to me are wrong, and the honest answer is a third thing.

(1) The two runs are NOT comparable, and I can say exactly why. The 1.005 pools day, night and worst-weather frames into one class per region. Doing that doubles intra-region scatter (32.24 -> 64.25) and collapses inter-centroid distance (99.95 -> 64.58), because a region's centroid becomes the average of a bright frame and a dark one. Split by condition, the SAME instrument on the SAME shipped file reads ours_day Fisher 3.10 / LOO 74.4%, ours_worst 3.53 / 82.0%, ours_night 1.99 / 33.3%. Against round 1's 3.01 / 66.7% on 39 day frames, the day world got BETTER, not worse.

(2) But 'not like-for-like' is not a defence, so I built the like-for-like myself. Morrowind's set is 9 regions x 4.33 images at chance 11.1%; ours is 13 x 9 at chance 7.7%; those Fishers were never comparable either. Matched design — 9 regions, 3 images each, 200 random draws, both populations, identical chance: ours_day 3.087 +/- 0.322 with LOO 77.5%; Morrowind 1.614 +/- 0.113 with LOO 24.2%. A7 passes, decisively. And ours_pooled comes out at 1.536 +/- 0.312, which is statistically indistinguishable from Morrowind's 1.614 +/- 0.113 — so the 'we are below Morrowind' reading survives only if our night frames are pooled and theirs are not. Morrowind's own frames are not single-condition either (mean L 35.7 +/- 14.6, min 5.5), but they are 39 opportunistic screenshots, not a deliberate one-third night sample.

(3) The bad number is real, it is just not the one on the label. What the pooled Fisher is actually reporting is that the night pass — shipped for the first time — fails RI-WLD04 M17 step 6's explicit bar of >=70% night accuracy, at 33.3% raw and 25.6% once exposure is removed. 'A region that is only identifiable in clear daylight is half-built' is the item's own sentence and it is the finding. Nothing about the day world regressed; a half of the world that had never been measured was measured and it failed.

(4) And the instrument is measuring the wrong thing anyway, which is the part neither reading anticipated. A 4x4 grid of mean CIELAB is satisfied by a colour grade. When I strip colour and exposure entirely and keep only silhouette and composition, ours_day falls from 74.4% to 30.8% while Morrowind falls from 25.6% to 17.9% — two-thirds of our separability is tint. That is why the machine says 74.4% and a human taking the same test says 50%, and it is why the biggest gap in this verdict is region identity rather than the road.

THE ROAD FIX HOLDS, WITH A COST. Zero offences over four tide phases and ten legs, recomputed by me from the terrain; the round-1 point at (2182.52, 2214.63) is dry land at 157.48 m; the crossing re-measures at 55.356 min / 6,642.1 m with mean 1.9998 m/s, so the hour still comes from distance and the route was not broken by the re-route. It did not simply raise the road and leave a wall — the player can walk off the embankment in all four directions — but it did raise the road: 17.52 m of fill at the worst point, 2,537 sampled shoulder points above 40 degrees, and a 58.6-degree longitudinal grade on THE CROSSING's first leg, with 21 'deck_spans' that exist only as JSON.

AR-3 — SEAM STERILITY: NOT STERILE. Three boundary-crossing interactions were observed firing. (a) The tide gates a road: lilmoth-archon measures 0.976 m at LOW and 1.456 m at HIGH, a Morrowind world-clock property deciding whether a Souls-side traversal exists, measured by me at all four phases. (b) The travel network gates on a Souls-side act: you cannot buy passage over a road you have not walked, and I watched 68 refusals become 39 purchases by walking four legs. (c) S18's third-person body is load-bearing for S25: the depth bands the water model now enforces (1.87 / 1.70 / 1.10 m/s) are meant to be read off the player's silhouette against the waterline, and the silhouette is there. A fourth is named and does not fire: danger_tier 1-5 on all thirteen regions, with entitiesLive 0.

SCORE MOVEMENT, FLAGGED PER SCORING.md §4. RI-TRV01 moves 0 -> 6 and RI-PRG07 moves 1 -> 6 in one wave. Both are >= 3 and both are therefore suspect by rule. I verified both with artifacts rather than reports: five modalities boarded, paid and rode with the player's gold falling 5000 -> 4862 (critic-b13-travel.json), and seven burden ratios swept with movement multipliers 1.0/0.9/0.72/0 measured off the capsule's realised speed (critic-misc-probe.json). These are real improvements, not method changes. RI-WLD04 moves 5 -> 3 in the other direction, and that IS a method change: round 1 could not take M17 because the pack was unshuffled, and it never ran M19. The regions did not get worse; the measurement got honest.

PIECE DECOMPOSITION, unchanged since round 1 and worth restating. Four of the ten assigned items (RI-CAM02, RI-AI05, RI-PRG06, RI-TRV01) judge camera rigs, enemy rosters, souls curves and transport that docs/PLAN.md assigns to W1-05, W1-06, W1-09 and W1-14. Restricted to the four items whose primary subject is a path this piece owns — RI-WLD01, RI-WLD04, RI-WLD07, RI-WLD10 — the mean is 4.5. That is a defect in the decomposition, not a defence of the piece, and the 3.5 stands.
